history.dynasty: Kadamba-Yadava (attributed to Kadamba queen Kamladevi / Hemadri Pandit tradition)
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 246 (Tambdi Surla Mahadev Temple) - same real temple. CSV town 'Sanguem' is the taluka; the temple stands at Tambdi Surla village (pin 403505, Sancordem area), Sanguem taluka, South Goa, in a clearing of the Bhagwan Mahaveer Wildlife Sanctuary. It is Goa's oldest surviving temple and its only intact Kadamba-Yadava structure, built of black basalt carried from the Deccan plateau, with no mortar - stones held by gravity and friction. Its remote forest location saved it from destruction during Muslim and Portuguese rule; legend attributes it to a Kadamba queen, Kamladevi (unverified). It is an ASI-protected Monument of National Importance and an active worship site, with subtle Jain-influenced motifs (kirtimukha, makara, kalasha) reflecting Kadamba-era religious syncretism.

name: Tambdi Surla Temple (Shri Mahadeva Temple)
town_description: Tambdi Surla is a remote forest village in Sanguem taluka, South Goa, inside the Bhagwan Mahaveer Wildlife Sanctuary near the Karnataka border, about 20 km from Mollem. It is a tiny settlement in dense Western Ghats forest known almost entirely for the 12th-century Mahadeva temple and nearby trekking trails and waterfalls.

travel.road: ~20 km from Mollem on forest roads via the sanctuary; private vehicle or taxi essential; sanctuary gates close ~6:30 PM

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (15-25 degC); Mahashivratri (Feb-March) for the main festival; early morning (7-9 AM) for tranquillity
